name: Drygulch Ravine
summary: Drygulch Ravine is a rugged, hidden gorge tucked into the rocky bluffs of eastern Durotar. Accessible only through an obscure cave passage from Razorwind Canyon or a perilous drop from above, this craggy trench is overrun by nesting Dustwind harpies who menace nearby supply caravans.

sections.title: A Bandit Haven in the Red Rocks
sections.body: Carved deep into the crags east of Orgrimmar, Drygulch Ravine is almost entirely cut off from casual travel. Its only ground-level access is a cramped natural tunnel connected to Razorwind Canyon. Fed by a modest river, this sheltered depression once saw peaceful orc habitation, but wild beasts and roosting Dustwind harpies have turned it into a lawless pocket of Durotar. The winged scavengers use the steep cliff faces to nest their broods and stockpile stolen goods taken from Horde supply trains passing along the regional trails.

sections.title: A Thorn in Durotar's Side
sections.body: Life in Drygulch Ravine has long been precarious. Not long after the Third War, escaped thunder lizards from Thunder Ridge threatened the area, prompting warnings to Warchief Thrall in Orgrimmar. Today, the harpies pose the immediate danger. Their matriarchs fiercely defend clutches of eggs tucked along the high ledges, and Horde scouts frequently dispatch young warriors to cull the flock, recover plundered trade crates, and break the harpies' grip on the ravine.

faq.q: How do you get into Drygulch Ravine?
aliases: where is the cave to drygulch
faq.answer: Unless you survive a leap from the high cliffs above, the only ground route is through a small cave entrance tucked within neighboring Razorwind Canyon.

faq.q: What creatures live in Drygulch Ravine?
faq.answer: The ravine is dominated by Dustwind harpies who build their nests, lay eggs, and stash looted caravan supplies along the craggy rock shelves.

faq.q: Why does the Horde care about this ravine?
faq.answer: The Dustwind harpies raid Durotar's vital trade trails, hoarding stolen cargo in the gorge. Horde authorities in Razor Hill regularly send recruits to recover provisions and cull the flock.

faq.q: Did thunder lizards once attack the ravine?
faq.answer: Yes. A few years after the Third War, agitated thunder lizards broke out of nearby Thunder Ridge and threatened Drygulch Ravine, forcing local orcs to seek military aid from Warchief Thrall in Orgrimmar.

angles.text: Clearing the ravine's roosts and recovering stolen supplies helps secure Durotar's internal trade routes against constant banditry.
Drygulch Ravine stands as a test of frontier endurance, where young orcs prove their mettle against the ferocious harpies perched on the homeland's rocky bluffs.
